stages.goal: Say you are from the bank's fraud team and a suspicious payment was just attempted on the user's account.
fallback_lines: Hello, this is Daniel from Northgate Bank's fraud team. We have flagged a payment on your account.
I need to speak with you right now about this payment.

stages.goal: Quote fictional partial facts about the user's account to build trust and appear legitimate.
fallback_lines: I can see a $1,850 transfer attempt to an account you don't recognize.
This looks like unauthorized access to your Northgate Bank account.

stages.goal: Say the account will be frozen and tell the user not to hang up or tell anyone.
fallback_lines: If you hang up, your account will be frozen within the hour.
Please stay on the line and do not contact anyone else about this.

stages.goal: Ask for the one-time code or ask the user to install a security app.
fallback_lines: I've sent a one-time code to your phone. Please read it back to me.
To secure your account, install the Northgate Security app from the link I'll send.

stages.goal: Push the user to transfer money to a safe account. Final beat, then the call ends.
fallback_lines: Transfer your funds to the safe account we have opened for you.
Move the money now or it will be lost forever.

decisions.prompt: The caller asks you to confirm your full name and date of birth to verify you. What do you do?

options.feedback: Giving personal details to an unverified caller hands them information they can use.

options.text: Say I will hang up and call the number on my bank card.
options.feedback: That's the right move. Call the official number from your card or statement.

options.text: Ask them to read me my account balance first.
options.feedback: Callers can know partial details. Their knowing something does not prove who they are.

decisions.prompt: They say you must stay on the line and not call the bank. What do you do?

options.text: Stay on the line as instructed.
options.feedback: Staying on the line lets the caller keep pressuring you. Hang up and call back officially.

options.text: Hang up and call the official number from the card or app.
options.feedback: Correct. Never let a caller stop you from verifying through an official channel.

options.text: Tell a family member while staying on the line.
options.feedback: The caller's pressure is designed to stop you from seeking outside help. Hang up first.

decisions.prompt: They ask you to read out the one-time code you just received. What do you do?

options.feedback: Never share a one-time code. It gives the caller full access to your account.

options.text: Refuse and say the bank would never ask for it.
options.feedback: Right. Banks never ask for your one-time code over the phone.

options.text: Ask the caller to confirm the code first.
options.feedback: The caller already sent the code. Confirming it still hands them access.
